-- Upgrades: pure data for the dropper / ore tier / speed / cash multiplier tree.
-- No requires, no side effects. Returns { list = {...}, byId = {...}, ores = {...}, starterCash = n }.

-- server purchase check, the tutorial text and the HUD "Next:" hint must all read cost from here.
-- Dropper 2 = 10 and Speed 1 (Fast Belt) = 22, matching the design doc, Config.STARTING_CASH (10)
-- and the tutorial text ("the pad costs $10").
--
-- BUDGET MATH
--   The first cube (Bronze) is worth 5 cash. The player starts with 10 cash, so the first buy
--   (Dropper 2, 10 cash) is affordable immediately after claiming a plot. After that, income is
--   5 cash/s (2 cubes per 2 s cycle x 5 cash), so every following purchase lands 4-24 s apart.
--   Total cost of all 10 upgrades:
--     10 + 22 + 60 + 150 + 300 + 500 + 800 + 1300 + 2200 + 4000 = 9342 cash
--   Income after each milestone (cubes per 2 s cycle x ore value x cash multiplier, per second),
--   and the approximate wait for the NEXT purchase at that income:
--     base                        1 x 5  x 1.0 / 2 =   2.5 /s   (Dropper 2 affordable immediately)
--     dropper2                    2 x 5  x 1.0 / 2 =   5   /s   (Speed 1, 22  -> ~4 s)
--     speed1                                           5   /s   (Silver, 60   -> ~8 s)
--     tier_silver                 2 x 12 x 1.0 / 2 =  12   /s   (Dropper 3, 150 -> ~12 s)
--     dropper3                    3 x 12 x 1.0 / 2 =  18   /s   (Cash x1.5, 300 -> ~17 s)
--     mult1 (x1.5)                3 x 12 x 1.5 / 2 =  27   /s   (Gold, 500 -> ~18 s)
--     tier_gold                   3 x 30 x 1.5 / 2 =  67.5 /s   (Speed 2, 800 -> ~12 s)
--     speed2                                          67.5 /s   (Dropper 4, 1300 -> ~19 s)
--     dropper4                    4 x 30 x 1.5 / 2 =  90   /s   (Cash x2, 2200 -> ~24 s)
--     mult2 (x2)                  4 x 30 x 2.0 / 2 = 120   /s   (Diamond, 4000 -> ~33 s)
--     tier_diamond                4 x 75 x 2.0 / 2 = 300   /s
--   (speed upgrades only shorten the trip to the collector.)
--
-- Effect shapes:
--   { kind = "dropper",  slots = n }   total active dropper slots after purchase
--   { kind = "tier",     tier = n }    ore tier every dropper spits out (index into ores)
--   { kind = "speed",    mult = x }    conveyor speed multiplier
--   { kind = "cashMult", mult = x }    collector cash multiplier
--
-- Optional presentation fields (read by the client for the purchase celebration):
--   label  = short headline string
--   popup  = RewardPopup text (shown with Win sting, shockwave ring and FOV punch for ore tiers)
--   color  = Color3 for the shockwave ring / popup (ore tiers)
--
-- Every `requires` points at an existing id, so pads reveal progressively.

local list = {
	{ id = "dropper2", name = "Dropper 2", cost = 10, requires = nil, effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 2 } },
	{ id = "speed1", name = "Speed 1", cost = 22, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 1.5 } },
	{
		id = "tier_silver",
		name = "Silver Ore",
		cost = 60,
		requires = "dropper2",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 2 },
		label = "Silver Ore",
		popup = "SILVER ORE! $12 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220),
	},
	{ id = "dropper3", name = "Dropper 3", cost = 150, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 3 } },
	{ id = "mult1", name = "Cash x1.5", cost = 300, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 1.5 } },
	{
		id = "tier_gold",
		name = "Gold Ore",
		cost = 500,
		requires = "tier_silver",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 3 },
		label = "Gold Ore",
		popup = "GOLD ORE! $30 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40),
	},
	{ id = "speed2", name = "Speed 2", cost = 800, requires = "speed1", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "dropper4", name = "Dropper 4", cost = 1300, requires = "dropper3", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 4 } },
	{ id = "mult2", name = "Cash x2", cost = 2200, requires = "mult1", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 2 } },
	{
		id = "tier_diamond",
		name = "Diamond Ore",
		cost = 4000,
		requires = "tier_gold",
		effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 4 },
		label = "Diamond Ore",
		popup = "DIAMOND ORE! $75 per cube",
		color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255),
	},

-- Indexed by tier.
local ores = {
	{ name = "Bronze", value = 5, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 127, 50), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Silver", value = 12, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Gold", value = 30, color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40), material = Enum.Material.Foil, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Diamond", value = 75, color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255), material = Enum.Material.Glass, sparkles = true },

local byId = {}
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do

end

-- Sanity check: every requirement must reference an existing upgrade id.
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do

return {

	byId = byId,
	ores = ores,
	-- Starter grant: matches Config.STARTING_CASH so the first upgrade (Dropper 2, 10) is affordable immediately.
	starterCash = 10,
}

## Problem
Playtest critique:
- starterCash is 10 and Dropper 2 costs 10, so the first pad is affordable at second 0. The player gets no earn-then-spend moment from the first collected cube. The playtest never recorded a purchase at all. (hint: Set starterCash to 0 (and keep Config.STARTING_CASH in sync) so the first two $5 cubes visibly fill the HUD goal bar before the Dropper 2 pad turns green. If playtest pacing needs it, set starterCash to 5. Keep Dropper 2 at cost 10 so the spec still holds.)

## Context
Game: Cube Cash Tycoon - Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!
Core loop: Each player gets a bright plot with a dropper that spawns a 1-cash cube every 2 seconds onto a conveyor. The conveyor carries cubes to a collector at the end, and the server adds each cube's value to the player's Cash leaderstat and destroys the cube. Two buy pads sit off to the side of the walking area: a second dropper for 25 cash and a faster conveyor for 50 cash. Touching a pad with enough cash buys the upgrade once, so income climbs and the numbers go up.
Acceptance: The map (baseplate and the player's plot with dropper, conveyor, collector and two buy pads) is built from parts at startup and the 'map_built' counter is 1; The player spawns on their plot within a few seconds, and 'plot_assigned' is 1; 'cubes_dropped' increases within the first 2 seconds and keeps increasing roughly every 2 seconds; 'cubes_collected' increases as cubes reach the collector, and the Cash leaderstat rises; Touching a buy pad with insufficient cash does nothing; with enough cash it deducts the cost once and increments 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought'; The HUD shows the current Cash and updates as it changes; Walking from spawn does not trigger the buy pads accidentally, and the cube count stays under the cap; No errors or warnings appear in the output; At startup the plaza (stone tiles, fountain, lamp posts, trees) and 6 plots in a ring exist; 'plaza_built' is 1, 'themes_built' is 6 and 'map_built' is 1; Each plot has a distinct theme floor material and color plus 3-5 decoration props (lollipops, lava cracks, crystals, palm trees, neon strips, cacti), and no part is default grey; rails, drop

# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Do not give starting cash equal to the first upgrade's price. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. Put it close to the claimed plot's spawn point, off the walking path, and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad or button pressed without enough cash needs a red flash, an audible buzz and a "Need $N" toast, debounced to about 1s. A silent denial confuses young players.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.
